name: Profound RF

lead: Profound is a radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system used in aesthetic clinics. People turn to it for firmer skin, softer wrinkles and smoother acne scars, which are the changes it is aimed at.

Fine needles enter the skin and deliver RF energy at depth, which prompts a healing response and collagen remodeling over the following weeks. Research on the device is mostly registered device studies, including cellulite, wrinkle and acne-scar studies and a 500-person feasibility study of the Profound Matrix system.

paras: It is performed in a clinic by a trained provider, usually as a short in-office session with numbing applied first. Results build gradually as collagen remodels, and people often combine it with other skin treatments or a sunscreen routine.

Redness and swelling after microneedling are expected for a few days. Infection is a concern when the procedure is done in unregulated settings with poor infection control. Device-specific safety findings are not summarized in the available sources.

lead: Profound is a radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system used in aesthetic medicine. It combines needle insertion into the skin with RF energy delivered at depth, and is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a hardmaxxing option for skin laxity, wrinkles and acne scarring. Microneedling in general is a cosmetic procedure in which sterile needles repeatedly puncture the skin to induce a healing response, also called collagen induction therapy [1].

Evidence specific to Profound consists mainly of registered device studies run through ClinicalTrials.gov, including studies of cellulite cartridges, wrinkle and acne-scar usability testing, and a 500-person feasibility study of the Profound Matrix system [2][3][4]. No peer-reviewed results are summarized here.
infobox: Skin laxity, wrinkles, acne scars, cellulite (per registered studies)

paras: Radiofrequency microneedling adds RF energy to the mechanical injury of needling, with the stated aim of tightening and remodeling tissue beneath the skin surface. Wikipedia's article on microneedling covers the general technique and notes uses for scarring and acne [1]. It does not discuss RF devices or specific brands.

ClinicalTrials.gov lists several Profound studies. A completed 2017 study with 31 participants evaluated Profound dermal and subcutaneous cartridges for cellulite [2]. A completed 2020 usability and feasibility study of the Profound Matrix system enrolled 193 people with wrinkles and mixed atrophic and hypertrophic acne scars [3]. A larger feasibility study of safety and performance began in 2022 with 500 participants and is listed as active, not recruiting, covering skin laxity and wrinkles [4]. A 2024 radiofrequency microneedling device study with six healthy participants was terminated [5].
These registry entries describe study designs and status; this article does not report outcome data from them.

timeline.event: Study of Profound cartridges for cellulite begins [2].
